jobs.title: Career Advance Internship at San Francisco International Airport
jobs.description: Employer: San Francisco International Airport - San Francisco International Airport Expires: 12/03/2026 Are you a motivated student or recent graduate looking to gain hands-on experience while working at one of the nation’s leading airports? SFO’s Career Advance Internships provide motivated individuals with an opportunity to gain valuable hands-on work experience, develop professional skills, and contribute to the day-to-day operations and initiatives of San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Interns are placed in one of several Airport offices and paired with an SFO mentor who provides guidance, support, and opportunities for professional growth through daily assignments and larger-scale projects. In addition to their host office experience, interns receive ongoing support from SFO’s Career Pathways Team and participate in professional development opportunities, including airport tours, networking opportunities with Airport leadership, workshops, and other activities designed to broaden their understanding of airport operations, strengthen their skills, and prepare them for future career opportunities. Below is the list of host offices participating:1. Airport Director’s Office: The Director's Office Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in administrative operations and executive-level support while developing skills in communication, organization, research, writing, and document management. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will contribute to front desk operations, administrative projects, correspondence, and day-to-day office activities while gaining exposure to executive leadership and organizational processes.2. Airfield Safety: The Airfield Safety Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in aviation safety, training program evaluation, and data analysis while supporting efforts to enhance SFO's Airport Movement Area Training Programs and reduce runway incursions. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will work alongside airport safety and training professionals to evaluate initial, recurrent, and specialized driver training programs, identify knowledge gaps, and explore opportunities for improvement. The intern will assist with researching Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) guidance, industry best practices, emerging training technologies, and training approaches used at other airports. The intern will also support the review and analysis of training records, operational incidents, and deviation data to identify trends and develop recommendations for improving training effectiveness and knowledge retention. Through these assignments, the intern will develop skills in research, data analysis, interviewing, technical writing, and program evaluation while gaining an understanding of aviation human factors, airfield safety principles, and continuous safety improvement.3. Aviation Security and Regulatory Compliance: The Aviation Security (AVSEC) Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in airport security operations and regulatory compliance while developing an understanding of the policies, procedures, and technologies that support a safe and secure airport environment. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will work alongside AVSEC professionals to support the analysis, investigation, and resolution of operational incidents, as well as the planning of airport construction projects within restricted and public areas. The intern will also gain exposure to security infrastructure by participating in the inspection and testing of access control and closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems while developing skills in research, problem-solving, documentation, and regulatory compliance.4. Career Pathways: The Career Pathways Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in workforce development, program coordination, and project management while supporting SFO's Career Pathways programs. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will assist with coordinating internship and fellowship activities, supporting participant onboarding and engagement, organizing professional development workshops and airport tours, and communicating with interns, mentors, host offices, and community partners.The intern will also support program administration by maintaining tracking systems, organizing documentation, collecting participant feedback, and preparing reports and presentations. Through short- and long-term projects, the intern will gain exposure to program evaluation, data management, process improvement, and stakeholder engagement while contributing to SFO's efforts to develop a skilled future aviation workforce.5.Facilities (Scheduling and Control): The Facilities Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in facilities operations, asset management, preventive maintenance planning, and process improvement while supporting the Airport's Enterprise Facilities Management (EFM) initiative and implementation of IBM Maximo. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will work alongside the Scheduling & Control Unit, maintenance planners, engineers, and skilled trades personnel to assist with collecting and validating asset information, maintaining equipment inventories, and supporting preventive maintenance and inspection programs. The intern will also gain exposure to digital inspection tools, maintenance planning systems, and data reporting by assisting with the development of inspection checklists, maintenance job plans, reports, and dashboards. Through these assignments, the intern will develop skills in data management, research, documentation, project coordination, and process improvement while gaining an understanding of how facilities management supports safe, efficient, and reliable airport operations.6. IT Digital Transformation: The IT Digital Transformation Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in business analysis, project management, change management, enterprise asset management, digital transformation, business process improvement, and data analytics while supporting SFO's implementation of IBM Maximo as part of the Airport's broader Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) initiative.Working alongside IT professionals, project teams, and business stakeholders, the intern will assist with gathering, analyzing, and documenting business requirements; supporting project planning and coordination activities; identifying operational gaps and opportunities for process improvement; and analyzing and visualizing data to support informed decision-making. The intern will also gain exposure to enterprise systems, system integrations, asset governance, organizational change management, and project delivery practices while contributing to efforts that improve data quality, streamline business processes, facilitate user adoption, and strengthen asset management capabilities across the Airport.This internship provides valuable experience in business analysis, project management, change management, stakeholder engagement, data analytics, and enterprise technology while supporting initiatives that drive operational excellence and digital innovation.7. Reprographics: The Reprographics Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in graphic design, print production, and administrative operations while supporting San Francisco International Airport's (SFO) reprographics services. Through guided learning and practical assignments, the intern will assist with developing and editing graphic design materials, preparing digital files for printing, and supporting the production of printed materials for various Airport divisions and initiatives.Working alongside reprographics professionals, the intern will gain exposure to the design and print production process, including project planning, layout and formatting, printing techniques, quality control, and coordination of print requests. The intern will also support day-to-day administrative activities, including organizing project files, maintaining records, tracking work requests, and assisting with general office coordination.Through short- and long-term projects, the intern will develop skills in visual communication, graphic design, print production, customer service, project coordination, and administrative support while contributing to SFO's internal communications and operational needs.8. Bureau of Planning & Environmental Affairs: The Planning and Environmental Affairs Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in airport planning and environmental affairs sections through guided learning and practical assignments.Environmental Affairs sectionThe Career Advance Intern will assist with regulatory compliance and reporting, natural resources management, and project coordination while supporting Airport maintenance and capital improvement projects. The intern will assist with gathering and analyzing environmental data, preparing documentation for federal and state environmental reviews, and supporting resource permit applications and regulatory submittals.The intern will also support implementation of SFO’s San Francisco Garter Snake (SFGS) Recovery Action Plan, including coordination and preparation of the calendar year 2027 work plan, project scheduling, environmental monitoring, documentation, and reporting in accordance with applicable permit requirements. Responsibilities will include supporting pre- and post-construction activities, participating in weekly project coordination meetings, and assisting with internal and external stakeholder engagement to inform the development of the next 10-year SFGS Recovery Action Plan.Airport Planning sectionThe Career Advance Intern will support a variety of airport planning studies and strategic initiatives by conducting research, data analysis, and documentation activities. The intern will assist with analyzing airport operational trends, passenger and facility data, and other planning metrics to help evaluate existing conditions and support future airport development efforts. Responsibilities may include preparing reports, presentations, maps, graphics, and other planning materials used to communicate findings and recommendations.Through these assignments, the intern will gain exposure to airport master planning, facilities planning, aviation forecasting, transportation planning, stakeholder coordination, and capital development processes while working closely with Airport Planning staff on projects that support the airport's long-term operational, infrastructure, and sustainability goals.9. Procurement Services: The Procurement Services Career Advance Intern will gain hands-on experience in public-sector procurement, contract administration, training coordination, and departmental operations while developing skills in communication, organization, data management, and project coordination .Under the guidance of Procurement Services staff, the intern will assist with coordinating training sessions and procurement meetings, including scheduling, room reservations, vendor and participant communications, and preparation of training materials. Responsibilities will also include maintaining training records, and supporting related administrative activities.The intern will gain exposure to procurement and contract administration by assisting with organizing contract documentation, tracking contracts and task orders, supporting small-dollar purchasing activities, maintaining vendor databases, and coordinating vendor outreach. Additional assignments may include maintaining departmental databases and tracking tools, compiling information for reports, organizing electronic records, and preparing procurement-related documents and correspondence.More detailed information on the Career Advance internship can be found here: Career Advance Program 2027 | San Francisco International Airport Internship Details:Schedule: 24-32 hours per week in-person, Monday-Friday between 8:00 a.m. -5:00 p.m.Duration: 12 months How to QualifyEducation:1. Possession of a high school diploma; AND2.Completion of at least 90 semester units or 135 quarter units from an accredited college or university by the appointment date.***Please attach a copy of your unofficial transcript when submitting your applicationApplicants must meet the minimum qualification by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

jobs.title: 2027 PAID SUMMER LEGAL INTERNSHIPS at Legal Services of the Hudson Valley
jobs.description: Employer: Legal Services of the Hudson Valley Expires: 12/04/2026 About Us For more than 50 years, Legal Services of the Hudson Valley (LSHV) has been providing free, high-quality legal counsel in civil matters when basic human needs are at stake, including eviction and foreclosure prevention, domestic violence, disability, elder law, healthcare, consumer fraud and more. Our services support almost 600,000 poor and low-income families and individuals who cannot afford an attorney in our seven-county service area. With the gap separating those who can and cannot afford legal representation widening each day, we work to ensure that everyone has equal access to justice, regardless of their ability to pay. As the only provider of comprehensive civil legal services in the lower and mid-Hudson Valley (Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess, Rockland, Orange, Ulster and Sullivan), LSHV is proud to have handled over 12,000 cases impacting over 27,000 household members including over 10,000 children last year. LSHV is made up of ten offices, and a dedicated and highly skilled staff of attorneys, paralegals, and administrative professionals. Legal Services of Hudson Valley is dedicated to building a highly skilled workforce that reflects the diverse communities we serve and where everyone feels supported to bring their authentic selves to work. We are committed to racial justice and promoting equity for all, and we continuously review and strengthen our processes and practices to support our staff, clients and the communities we serve. Respect is a cornerstone of relationships among our staff. Our employee resource groups are self-directed and provide a space for members to support one another and their shared vision. We encourage applications from people of all identities and backgrounds. Fellowship Description LSHV will host 10 law student fellows in our housing units and 10 law student fellows in our general and/or other practice area units. Through these fellowships, LSHV will train the next generation of social justice lawyers, giving them both practical litigation experience and an understanding of the factors that create disadvantages for low-income individuals and families. While helping LSHV attorneys and staff serve clients, law fellows will receive training, mentorship, support, and skill development and engage in advocacy. Work may include client interviewing, issue spotting, legal research and writing, preparing court documents, accompanying attorneys and clients to court, and appearing in court under a student practice order. Housing Unit Fellows will help our clients to maintain the basic human and legal right to live in habitable housing and lend support to LSHV’s efforts to challenge landlord intimidation and harassment. General Practice Fellows will assist our staff attorneys in a variety of practice areas, including family law and domestic violence, housing, veterans’ benefits, public benefits, consumer debt, disability, and/or immigration law. Details 10-weekfellowship duration; 35 hours per work week required (5-day week, Mon – Fri) $8,000 stipend with 5 days paid time off (PTO) Fellows will be placed in LSHV offices throughout our service area, including White Plains, Yonkers, Mount Vernon, Peekskill, Poughkeepsie, New Windsor, Goshen, Nanuet, Monticello, and Kingston. Fellows will be loaned laptops during the summer for conducting LSHV business. Housing, transportation, work-related, and other fellowship expenses will be the law student's responsibility. LSHV will provide office parking where applicable. At the conclusion of the summer, fellows may be required to provide feedback concerning their experience, the substance of which may be reproduced in full or in part in LSHV materials. Eligibility Open to law students enrolled in a U.S. law school who will have completed two years of law school by May 2027 or are graduating in 2027. Must not have previously accepted an LSHV Paid Summer Legal Fellowship (previously titled LSHV Paid Summer Legal Internship). Must be able to work several days per week in person in the office where placed (our offices are hybrid, subject to disability-related reasonable accommodations. Ability to travel to the office where placed and other locations, such as courts, as needed. Application Timeline All materials must be submitted by Monday, December 21, 2026, at 11:59 pm (ET) Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered. Applicants selected for interviews will be notified in early January 2027. Finalists will be notified in early February 2027. Required Submissions Applications will be evaluated based upon review of the following: Complete Online Application with preferred office locations and practice areas Unofficial Law School Transcript Current Resume One legal writing sample on any topic (5-page limit) Statement of Interest (typed, double-spaced) Describe your commitment to public interest law and/or direct legal services, and what you hope to gain from LSHV’s Summer Internship Program. Please explain why you are interested in the practice area(s) you have preference in your application. You may include information such as personal experience, prior jobs, volunteer experience or internships and what you learned from them, as well as future career plans and professional goals. (750-word max) Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please email us at accommodate@lshv.org or call 914-949-1305 This email is created exclusively to assist disabled job seekers whose disability prevents them from being able to apply online. Only messages left for this purpose will be returned.

jobs.title: Winter Internship at Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, AFL-CIO
jobs.description: Employer: Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, AFL-CIO Expires: 12/04/2026 Who we are:HTC is the union for hotel and gaming workers in New York and New Jersey. We are widely recognized as the most powerful union in this industry in the world, with the best contracts. Our largely immigrant membership enjoys a middle class lifestyle, free family healthcare, the ability to retire with a pension. The children of our members have the opportunity to go to college and become professionals because of their parents’ hard work. This is unheard of in an industry where workers are generally exploited and living in poverty.Unlike most unions, our membership is expanding, and in the last ten years our membership has grown from 25,000 to over 40,000. In state and local politics, we are famous for “punching above our weight.” That’s because our membership loves their union and actively volunteers more than most union members.If you want to fight for social justice and win, this is the best place to do it.This role:The Winter Internship will take place from Monday, January 4th – Friday, January 22nd at our office in Midtown, Manhattan. During this 3-week internship, interns will gain hands-on exposure to different departments and roles within the organization. Interns will attend in-person grievance meetings and sit in on union-management negotiations with our contract enforcement team. Interns will also go into the field with our member mobilization team, traveling from shop to shop to communicate with members about pressing issues and mobilize them to upcoming union events. Interns will also work closely with the communications department, writing articles to report on union victories and events and working on other media projects requiring creativity and persuasiveness.This position is ideal for students with a passion for social justice, strong writing abilities, and the desire to learn.Qualifications:Demonstrated commitment to social justice;Ability to communicate respectfully and comfortably with people from diverse backgrounds;Ability to write persuasively, clearly, and creatively;Desire and ability to learn quickly and grow into positions of greater responsibility;Thorough attention to details;Ability to multitask, work efficiently, be well organized and reliable;Resourcefulness and talent for problem-solving;Persistence and determination;Loyalty to the organization, with a sense of integrity.Extra consideration will be given for ANY of the following qualifications:Bilingual (in addition to English), especially in Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, Vietnamese, Russian, Polish or Bengali;Strong computer skills and the ability to quickly learn new computer programs;Talent for photography, videography, and/or media design;Experience working in the hotel, restaurant, hospitality, or other service industries.Hours:35 hours/weekPay:$20Location:Midtown, Manhattan (in-person)How to Apply:In addition to a resume and references, applicants must include a cover letter. The cover letter should be clear and concise and explain which position you are applying for, the specific reasons for your interest in the position, and specify (with appropriate explanation) which of each of the listed qualifications you possess and which ones you do not possess. The cover letter, resume, and references should be emailed to: careers@nyhtc.org, with the subject line “Winter Internship #INT#”.The Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, AFL-CIO, is an equal opportunity employer. All persons regardless of age, race, ethnicity, gender, religious affiliation and sexual orientation are encouraged to apply.

jobs.description: Employer: National Park Service, De Soto National Memorial Expires: 12/04/2026 Community Volunteer Ambassador – AmeriCorps Conservation Legacy Program: Stewards Individual Placements Site Location: De Soto National Memorial 8300 Desoto Memorial Hwy, Bradenton, FL 34209 Terms of Service: • Start Date: 2/22/2027 • End Date: 2/4/2028 • AmeriCorps Slot Classification: 1700 Hours (50 Weeks) Purpose: Stewards Individual Placements (Stewards), a program of Conservation Legacy, provides individuals with AmeriCorps service and career opportunities to strengthen communities and preserve our natural resources. Participants serve with federal agencies, tribal governments, and nonprofits to provide institutional capacity, develop community relationships, and support ecosystem health. The Community Volunteer Ambassador (CVA) Program combines the strength of a national leader in conservation service with the National Park Service to train emerging leaders to assist park units in building lasting connections to communities. De Soto National Memorial is a 26-acre National Park Service site on Shaw’s Point in Bradenton, Florida. The park preserves a coastal landscape of mangrove wetlands, sandy shoreline, and upland forest while interpreting thousands of years of local history. Visitors can explore the Memorial Trail, Camp Uzita, and exhibits examining Indigenous communities, Hernando de Soto’s 1539 expedition, and the expedition’s lasting effects on the peoples and landscapes of the American Southeast. Description of Duties: The Community Volunteer Ambassador (CVA) supports the mission of De Soto National Memorial by strengthening connections between the park and the surrounding community. The CVA assists with recruiting, onboarding, and retaining volunteers who support park programs, special events, interpretation, and resource stewardship activities. The CVA develops and maintains relationships with community organizations, schools, civic groups, and partner agencies to expand public engagement and volunteer opportunities. Responsibilities include conducting outreach presentations, representing the park at community events, and promoting volunteer opportunities through various communication channels. The CVA also coordinates and tracks volunteer schedules, assists with event staffing, and supports volunteer recognition efforts. In collaboration with park staff and partners, the CVA schedules, attends, and participates in community stakeholder meetings to foster partnerships, identify collaborative opportunities, and enhance awareness of park programs, resources, and initiatives. Through volunteer engagement and community outreach, the CVA helps build lasting connections that support conservation, education, and stewardship at De Soto National Memorial. Based on our event planning document, the park regularly works with partners such as the Friends of De Soto and local community organizations, making stakeholder engagement and volunteer coordination key components of the position. Responsibilities: • Volunteer Recruitment o Review current volunteer recruitment strategies o Serve with park volunteer coordinators on methods to improve volunteer recruitment o Devise multimedia/ social media strategies and campaigns for volunteer recruitment o Attend offsite events and programs with the purpose in implementing these volunteer recruitment strategies • Community Outreach o Review current community outreach programs and look for ways to improve and prepare for offsite community events and outreach. o Schedule and attend outside community events for the purpose of increasing park outreach and volunteer recruitment. • Gateway Community Involvement o Review current park gateway community and shareholder strategies. o Improve Park gateway community relationships. o Create strategies and identify new possible park partnerships and gateway communities. Qualifications: • Must have completed or is currently enrolled in a bachelor's degree seeking program. • Great communications skillsexperience with Microsoft office products, CANVA, and Adobe products (photoshop, acrobat) • Social media experience in writing and editing posts in Facebook, Instagram, X, and YouTube. • Willing to serve with close knit team. • United States citizen, United States national, or a lawful permanent resident alien • Applicants must be between ages of 18-30 years old, or up to 35 for veterans, based on Public Land Corps Act of 1993 authorizing this AmeriCorps opportunity. • Has received a high school diploma or equivalency certificate; or has not dropped out of elementary or secondary school to enroll as an AmeriCorps participant, and agrees to obtain a high school diploma or its equivalent prior to using the education award • Agrees to provide information to establish eligibility and to complete a National Service Criminal History Check. Preferred Qualifications • Local applicants in area housing preferred. • Has current Driver's License. • Public Speaking • Social Media • Effective communication skills • Takes initiative with minimal supervisionwilling to learn and try new things • CPR/AED/First Aid training

jobs.title: COLLEGE CO-OP MSD/COMPLIANCE SERVICES DIVISION (LABORATORY) at City of Cincinnati
jobs.description: Employer: City of Cincinnati Expires: 12/05/2026 MSD DIVISION OF COMPLIANCE SERVICES - LABORATORY Mission: To establish a partnership with colleges and universities, exposing as many students as possible to employment opportunities in the Wastewater Industry and help them become experienced professionals in the next generation workforce.Purpose: To attract and cultivate bright and energetic college students and maintain ongoing partnerships with colleges and universities. It is our goal to expose these students to applied laboratory practices, as well as career opportunities in water resource management and the environmental sciences. The Co-op program also serves as a recruitment tool to assist the Compliance Services Division (CSD), Laboratory section in hiring full-time personnel. Overview: The co-op student will be assigned to specific areas of the laboratory to participate in wet weather projects, special studies, and/or daily routine testing. Under the supervision of a chemist, co-ops will be exposed to various tasks performed in the laboratory and on the analytical equipment utilized. The CSD Laboratory program strives to reinforce the knowledge and skills the students have learned in the classroom and to build on those skills in a setting that provides "hands-on" instruction and experience.Expectations: The Co-op students will be assigned to the Nutrient, Metals, and Sample Check-in Units where they will be trained in analyzing treatment plant NPDES permit samples, process control, wet weather, industrial waste, and/or special studies samples. They will be trained to perform a variety of analyses which may include sample receiving process, ammonia, nitrite and nitrate, total phosphorus, total orthophosphate, total Kjeldahl nitrogen, biochemical oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, alkalinity, total hardness, and suspended, total and dissolved solids. They will also be trained in running bacteriological samples for fecal coliform and E. coli analysis. Many of these procedures will involve the use of analytical equipment. They will learn the proper Quality Control to be run in analyzing these samples. They will also be trained in using the LIMS data entry program.Learning Milestones: Lab/Project orientation (week 1)Pertinent instruction for equipment or methodologies employed (week 1-4)Periodic status report (week 5-11)Completion of project/report out (week 12)All studies have been previously designed, and each student will be assigned to a specific study as his/her primary project.If the student has done a previous term at MSD, the project will be a continuation of that work.In addition to their primary project, students will be expected to perform other laboratory tasks and help in other areas as assistance is needed.The CSD lab attempts to expose students to all facets of laboratory analysis during the term. **Co-Ops may be required to work Tuesday-Saturday, day shift** HR Contact: Jerrold Ware, Jerrold.Ware@cincinnati-oh.gov

jobs.title: Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator at Polk County Conservation
jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 12/05/2026 The Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator plays a vital role in advocating for and enhancing outdoor recreation opportunities within Polk County Conservation. This position focuses on expanding Veteran’s programming, youth mental health initiatives, and enhancing current Equestrian Center program offerings. AmeriCorps Volunteers serving with the Equestrian Center will have dual enrollment in the Youth Mental Health Corps (YMHC) that is a nationwide initiative. Participants gain valuable practical skills through professional trainings and certification programs. The YMHC program is limited to individuals who are between the ages of 18-24; persons outside of that age range are ineligible for enrollment. This position is supportive and preventative in nature, not clinical. Volunteers do not provide therapy, counseling, diagnoses, or independent crisis intervention, nor are they expected to manage mental health emergencies beyond their training and comfortability. Instead, they help connect youth with appropriate staff and resources while contributing to a supportive outdoor environment. Through this service, Volunteers advance Polk County Conservation’s mission by making outdoor recreation and conservation education more accessible and meaningful for local youth, while helping foster the development of social connections and supportive experiences that contribute to the well-being of Polk County residents. One Quarter-Time Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($6,270) paid equally over the course of 450 hours of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon successful completion ($1,956.35) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. This position is Quarter-Time; Volunteers will serve a minimum of 450 hours over the course of 32 weeks, serving a minimum of 10 hours/week from January to May and a minimum of 24 hours/week from June to August. This posting is not a direct position of Polk County Conservation, and successful applicants will not be employees of Polk County. Successful applicants will not be subject to terms and conditions of Polk County employment and will not be eligible for any employee benefits provided by Polk County. However, these positions will be serving with Polk County Conservation, a host site of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program, and will be subject to AmeriCorps rules, benefits, and federal requirements. Volunteer Schedule January to May January program orientation and YMHC trainings Volunteer will spend a minimum of 10 hours/week participating in position-specific orientation and trainings. Some elements of the orientation and training can be completed via teleservice, but requires prior approval from Program Coordinator February program sessions begin: Monday evenings 4pm-8pm; Volunteer will complete YMHC tasks to meet the minimum of 10 hours/week June to August Summer youth programming sessions begin: Monday-Thursday 7am-2pm; 24 hours/week A 30-minute meal break will be allocated to the volunteer if they serve five consecutive hours in one service day; these 30 minutes cannot be counted towards the required 450 service hours Every service day will include one 15-minute break; additional breaks must be taken if the temperature is above 85 degrees Volunteer may serve during special events that take place on some weekends A minimum of two weeks’ notice will be given to Volunteer prior to the event occurring Volunteer will be allowed to flex hours during the week if there is an event occurring over the weekend to promote a healthy workload * Volunteers must not serve any hours on the major federal holidays – New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day. This includes checking emails, self-directed training, or teleservice. If the Host Site is open on one of these holidays and volunteers are expected to serve, the site supervisor should work with Program to gain approval for this volunteer service prior to the holiday. For any of the other federal holidays, including MLK Day, Presidents Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans Day, Host Sites will communicate expectations of volunteer service in advance. If the Host Site is closed on one of more of those lesser holidays (including the day after Thanksgiving or Christmas eve) or the Host Site recognizes other workdays when major federal holidays fall on weekend days, volunteers should not check their email, complete timesheets, or do teleservice on those days either unless they follow the procedure above. Sick or personal leave, and holidays is allowed, but such time off does not count towards the required number of hours needed to successfully complete the term of service. There are additional benefits offered if the volunteer has a compelling personal circumstance. The Quarter-Time Equestrian Center Programming Facilitator will receive two weeks of comprehensive training focused on the Jester Park Equestrian Center. Volunteers will become familiar with the facility, current equine services offered, current public outreach efforts, basic equine husbandry, fundamentals of speech to communicate with program attendees, and basics of program development. Volunteers will continue to receive on-the-job training outside of the first two weeks to improve their understanding of the changing needs of the public demographic that utilizes the Jester Park Equestrian Center. All participants in the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Youth Mental Health Corps Program that serve around youth or vulnerable adults are required to complete the following trainings: CPR/AED and first aid certification through the American Heart Association via online modules and an in-person practical skills test Mental Health First Aid Iowa DHS Mandatory Reporter Training ACEs 360 Volunteers may select between two YMHC workforce pathways based on their personal career goals. Community Health Worker: Public health for community health workers training (12 hours total) - required Youth mental health foundations training (2 hours total) - required School-based Mental Health Navigator: Volunteers enrolled in this pathway must select a minimum of one of the listed programs to meet the minimum requirements. Direct support professional behavioral and mental health certificate through DMACC (54 hours total) Registered behavioral technician certificate through University of Kansas (40 hours total) Requires additional registration for exam and passing of exam to receive certificate Paraeducator certification program (90 hours total) Additional Optional Trainings: Motivational Interviewing (2 hours total) School Mental Health Training through University of Iowa (multiple module options to choose from) Iowa Area Education Agencies (catalogue of additional trainings) Community Health Worker Specialization Trainings – must complete initial community health worker trainings Maternal Health Training (6 hours total) Mental Health Training (4.5 hours) Essential Functions: Develop and facilitate deliverable mental health programming that centers around outdoor recreation and the outdoors – primary audience of individuals between the ages of 13-24 Volunteers may also create handouts, infographics, social media videos, blog posts, or other forms of public resources for education and advocacy of mental health topics Volunteers will receive access to Canva for the creation of deliverables as well as a Google account for the development of program offerings All public deliverables must be approved by the Polk County Conservation Community Outreach staff before it can be utilized with Polk County residents Provide knowledgeable support to Polk County Conservation staff when navigating behavior management of program participants The Volunteer will utilize the information and skills developed from the training they complete and will provide appropriate resources to program participants as needed Establish a resource list that can be distributed to Polk County staff, community members, and other local organizations Design and facilitate a minimum of one equine-assisted service tailored to the needs and interests of Veterans and youth demographics during service term The volunteer-developed program will be focused on improving the emotional regulation and well-being of community members through the use of horses Facilitate and manage professional connections with Veteran service organizations and healthcare providers in the Polk County area to identify community members who could benefit from equine-assisted services and outdoor recreation opportunities The volunteer is responsible for communicating with partner organizations via email and phone about program opportunities to share with persons that utilize respective services The volunteer is responsible for promoting the program opportunity to partner organizations and prospective partner organizations to increase the number of individuals that the program positively impacts Assist with the promotion of the program by collecting photos of consenting program participants during programming to utilize for social media posts and for use on the Jester Park Equestrian Center website Work closely with full-time Equestrian Staff to develop, enhance, and diversify program offerings by incorporating new activities, therapeutic riding opportunities, and community outreach initiatives to better serve the needs and interests of the community Educate program participants on the physical and mental health benefits of equine-assisted activities and the therapeutic value of outdoor recreation Monitor program participant progress and outcomes through ongoing assessment and evaluation of program effectiveness through participant check-ins and surveys Non-Essential Functions: Engage in professional development opportunities to enhance knowledge and skills related to the environment, mental health, or youth management Record and maintain data such as number of program participants, type of program offered, location, average age of individuals, activity completed, etc. Conduct public surveys to determine how to effectively support Polk County residents when it comes to navigating mental health challenges and biases Volunteers may engage in other allowable activities that are not specifically outlined in the position description but that support the AmeriCorps program design and that will help the Program meet its goals. Under no circumstances will volunteers be asked to perform prohibited activities. Desired Skills/Qualifications: In pursuit of a Bachelor’s degree in psychology, human services, education, environmental science, outdoor recreation, or other related field AND/OR interest in providing support for community members navigating mental health challenges Comfortable working around horses of varying sizes and basic knowledge of equine-based recreation Experience working with children Passion for utilizing outdoor recreation for the purposes of improving mental health in a non-clinical format Knowledge or awareness of present-day mental health challenges Comfortability with public speaking and presenting programming independently Effective communication and interpersonal skills Eligibility Criteria: Be between the ages of 18 to 24 during the duration of the service term; persons outside of this age range are ineligible for the position at this time Pass a national service criminal history check prior to first day of service Hold one of the following citizenship statuses: US citizen, US national, or lawful permanent resident Possess a valid driver’s license and previous driving experience: Candidate must be comfortable with driving on all road types (gravel, grass, highways, rural, and city roads) Candidate must be comfortable driving in any environmental conditions (daytime, nighttime, rain, fog, sleet, ice, and snow) Candidate must be willing to drive to any location within Polk County, Iowa Candidate must pass a motor vehicle record check before they can operate any county vehicle Candidates with limited driving experience may be considered on a case-by-case basis Benefits: Education Award received upon successful completion of their term of service. Living Allowance Childcare coverage if the volunteer qualifies Housing opportunities provided by Polk County Conservation upon request Student loan forbearance and interest payments for eligible loans Certification in CPR/AED and first aid Mental Health First Aid Training Iowa DHS Mandatory Reporter Training ACEs 360 Training Performance Evaluation & Reporting Requirements: Volunteer Performance Evaluation requirements during the term Regular bi-weekly submission of volunteer timesheets Regular weekly submission of project data from each task a volunteer works on Daily progress reports to Polk County Conservation staff

You will help identify, analyze, and resolve quality, safety, and ergonomic challenges by researching potential solutions, evaluating alternatives, and assisting with implementation and long-term sustainment. This role offers meaningful exposure to real-world manufacturing environments and the opportunity to see your ideas translated into production-ready solutions.This position reports to the Manufacturing Engineering Manager and is an onsite role based in Germantown, Wisconsin, with opportunities to support projects at the Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin facility as well. floorBuild experience collaborating with cross-functional teams such as operations, quality, and maintenanceStrengthen professional skills in problem-solving, technical documentation, and cause analysis, fishbone diagrams, and statistical process control to diagnose and solve production issues.Monitor and analyze production data to identify opportunities for process improvement and documentation, such as standard operating procedures, process flow diagrams, and equipment specifications.Provide training and support to shop floor team members to ensure consistent understanding and execution of processes.Support the establishment of labor standards, product costing, and design of manufacturing processes.Collaborate with other departments, such as Operations, Quality, You will be required to work in the office at the Germantown location (Monday – Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. jobs.title: CDC Global Immunization and Polio Eradication Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/06/2026 Description*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.CDC Office and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is one of the major operation components of the Department of Health and Human Services. CDC protects America from health, safety and security threats, both foreign and in the U.S. Whether diseases start at home or abroad, are chronic or acute, curable or preventable, human error or deliberate attack, CDC fights disease and supports communities and citizens to do the same. CDC increases the health security of our nation. As the nation’s health protection agency, CDC saves lives and protects people from health threats. To accomplish its mission, CDC conducts important science and provides health information that protects our nation against expensive and dangerous health threats, and responds when these arise.Research Project: You will participate in a mentored fellowship with CDC’s Global Immunization Division (GID) focused on the scientific and public health approaches associated with global polio eradication. Through interactions with CDC technical personnel, you will learn about strategic, analytical, epidemiologic, and communication approaches used in polio eradication, including preparedness for and response to poliovirus outbreaks. As learning opportunities arise, you may also gain exposure to broader emergency preparedness and response approaches, including those used within CDC’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and Incident Management Structure (IMS).You will learn how technical and regional teams collaborate on global polio eradication activities; gain experience analyzing and synthesizing epidemiologic, programmatic, and outbreak-related information; and develop an understanding of how briefings, updates, and other informational materials communicate scientific findings. You will also strengthen collaboration skills through interactions across CDC programs and gain insight into partnerships involving Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) organizations and U.S. Government counterparts.You may gain mentored research experience related to outbreak preparedness and response, including analysis of outbreak and response data, examination of response-planning approaches, and research on guidance documents and information systems associated with outbreak readiness. Additional learning opportunities may include gaining familiarity with analytical tools and resources used to assess preparedness and observing or participating in educational and research activities related to polio outbreak response alongside experienced epidemiologists and other technical personnel.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will strengthen skills in applied epidemiology, data analysis, global immunization program approaches, outbreak preparedness and response research, and scientific communication. You will gain experience analyzing and interpreting epidemiologic and outbreak-related information, learn how scientific evidence informs public health practice, and develop an understanding of the epidemiologic, analytical, and collaborative approaches used in global polio eradication and emergency preparedness.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Monica Fleming (njl9@cdc.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: January 11, 2027. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be between January 2027 - September 2027, but may be renewed upon recommendation of CDC and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: Stipend rates may vary based on numerous factors, including opportunity, location, education, and experience. If you are interviewed, you can inquire about the exact stipend rate at that time and if selected, your appointment offer will include the monthly stipend rate.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens, Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR), and foreign nationals. Non-U.S. citizen applicants should refer to the Guidelines for Non-U.S. Citizens Details page of the program website for information about the valid immigration statuses that are acceptable for program participation.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and CDC. Participants do not become employees of CDC, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility, including but not limited to, poliovirus requirements (e.g. immunization, testing prior to laboratory access).Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process please email CDCrpp@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received or be currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in one of the relevant fields. Preferred skills:Graduate-level training or equivalent experience in public health, epidemiology, global health, immunization, infectious diseases, emergency management, or a related field.Experience analyzing epidemiologic, surveillance, programmatic, or operational data.Familiarity with infectious disease prevention, vaccination programs, outbreak response, emergency preparedness, or public health programs.Ability to synthesize complex information into concise briefings, reports, presentations, dashboards, and other decision-support items.Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information to diverse audiences.Ability to collaborate with domestic and international partners, manage multiple priorities, act independently, and adapt to evolving program needs.Stipend$5,439.25 MonthlyPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree received within the last 60 months or currently pursuing.
